problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration, measured in ${\text{m/s}}^{2},$ given by the function $a(t)=3+8t-3{t}^{2}$, where $t$ is the time in seconds. If the particle has velocity $v=-1\,\text{m/s}$ when $t=0\,\text{s}$, calculate the speed of the particle at the moment $t=2\,\text{s}.$

feedback.problem:
A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration, measured in ${\text{ft/s}}^{2},$ given by the function $a(t)=8{t}^{3}-6{t}^{2},$ where $t$ is the time in seconds. Find the speed of the particle at the moment $t=3\,\text{s}$ given that the particle has velocity $v=-4\,\text{ft/s}$ when $t=0\,\text{s}.$

The speed at the moment $t=3\,\text{s}$ is
{{field-1}} $\text{ft/s}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\text{d}t \\  & =\int (8{t}^{3}-6{t}^{2})\text{d}t \\  & =2{t}^{4}-2{t}^{3}+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v(0)=-4.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}-4 & =2({0}^{4})-2({0}^{3})+C \\ -4 & =0+C \\ C & =-4.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity $v$ of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t)=2{t}^{4}-2{t}^{3}-4.$

We evaluate the velocity at time $t=3\,\text{s}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(3) & =2({3}^{4})-2({3}^{3})-4 \\  & =2(81)-2(27)-4 \\  & =162-54-4 \\  & =104\,\text{ft/s}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since the speed is equal to $|v(t)|,$ we conclude that the speed of the particle is $104\,\text{ft/s}.$
